issue_context.title: UptimeRobot changed the API rate limits making the current integration useless (for the free plan)
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The Problem:
On Monday, July 26th UptimeRobot introduced a change in its API rate limits. 
All Free Plan accounts are now bounded to 10 requests/minute what makes the current integration useless because it is performing much more API requests than the limit.

The solution:
Not sure. But adding a new parameter to select the refresh frequency will help. (scan_interval). 

I'm not sure if the number of API requests depends on the number of monitors or we can pull all monitors with one single API request.




### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

ALL versions

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

UptimeRobot

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/uptimerobot/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Error on the log:
"Failed to get new state"
```


### Additional information

Email received from UptimeRobot:

```
Hi,

on Monday, July 26th we’ll be deploying a change in our API rate limits. 

All Free Plan accounts will be bound to 10 requests/minute. 

PRO Plan rate limits will be based on the number of monitors in your plan (with a maximum value of 1,000 requests/minute). 

This means if you have the 50-monitor PRO plan, you’re bound to 50 requests/minute, for 100 monitors it’s 100 requests/minute, etc. 

Thank you.

Regards,
Kristian from UptimeRobot
```

review_comments: Inconsistent return value. All return statements should return a value explicitly if any return statement returns a value. Return `None` here.
We can remove `True` if we remove `async_update`.
Remove `async_update` and implement `_handle_coordinator_update` callback method or just the `is_on` property.

This function can be replaced with a generator expression and `next` with default None.
```py
monitor = next(
    (monitor for monitor in monitors if monitor["id"] == monitor_id),
    None
)
```
The coordinator is set as an attribute by the coordinator entity.
We could move the wrapper function outside `async_update_data` to avoid defining the function every update.
